5 Lightroom Moves for Warm Cinematic Tones ✍︎
 
Walking through the Lightroom adjustments I actually use to get that soft, warm, cinematic feel with real depth to it.
 
These aren’t plug-and-play settings. Every photo comes with different light and colour, so you’ll need to adjust based on what you’re working with.
 
Think of this as a window into how I approach editing and the general ranges I stick to. The point is understanding how warmth, balance, and contrast work together to set the mood, not copying numbers exactly.
 
Edit with intention instead of chasing exact sliders, and a consistent cinematic look starts coming naturally.
 
Want the full Lightroom breakdown + exact slider ranges?

Cropping doesn’t get enough credit. It’s one of the simplest ways to turn an average frame into something that actually holds attention, tightening the composition, guiding focus, and revealing details you’d otherwise scroll past.
 
If you want the freedom to crop without losing quality, shoot RAW and lean on a high-megapixel body. It gives you that extra bit of room to play with in post.

Those 70/30 odds suddenly don’t sound so funny. 🥲🧊

Falling through wild ice is no joke. The initial cold water shock can affect your breathing and ability to react. So it’s important to know what to do and not panic! 😱 

This was part of a wild ice safety course with @lucmehl , where we intentionally practised falling through the ice and getting ourselves back out.

⚠️ Important context: this was done in a controlled environment, with professional supervision and a group. Please don’t recreate this on your own.

Wild ice is incredible. Learning how to stay safe on it is part of the sport too. 🤍 remember this when you go out this winter!

Jewels of the Arctic. Two weeks across East Greenland and Svalbard, aboard @aurora_expeditions Greg Mortimer. 

Recounting this dream trip, frame by frame! 
 Pictured above is one of the countless highlights from the voyage. We came across this female polar bear on an ice floe, over forty kilometres out to sea (they are incredibly powerful swimmers). Beside her, a seal kill. What a moment.

#AuroraPartner #AuroraExpeditions #Greenland #Svalbard #WorldPhotographyDay 

A rosy, foggy first glimpse of East Greenland after a day at sea crossing the Denmark Strait.

The golden morning light lasts forever here. 

Our first stop, anchored off Tasiilaq. One of the most secluded and beautiful towns I’ve ever seen. Icebergs drifting past your living room… just casually.

Home to around 1,800 residents, it’s the largest settlement in East Greenland. We wandered through town with local guides, admiring the vibrant houses and serenity of everyday life. 

Iced coffee, Greenland style.

Every day is an adventure with @aurora_expeditions - zipping around on Zodiacs for a closer look at the ice. Jagged peaks of over a thousand metres in the backdrop. 

Amongst all the grandeur and breathtaking scenery, unassuming sea grass. Very angelic looking.

Saw so much ice during our time cruising up the east coast of Greenland. At its most pure and dense it bounces back blue light and reflects these colours. 🧊🩵

After a couple of days at sea, we were greeted in Svalbard by the walruses. Those tusks!

Enjoying the afternoon rays on our balcony as we venture up the northwestern side of Svalbard’s archipelago. 

Appreciating not just the form of ice on this trip, but water too.

@aurora_expeditions guides are a wealth of knowledge and from the moment the lecture finished on ‘Arctic botany’, I had my eye out for the elegant, lantern-esque Polar Campion. I finally spotted them on the tundra during one of our last outings. 

The ancient landscapes of the High Arctic.

Capping off another mind-blowing day in Svalbard, sailing into a bay where we had 180 degrees of glaciers. 

At this point, almost two weeks in, feeling like a real Arctic explorer. 🤓

Land of ice? Not really. 

These are drone shots using my @dji.philippines @djiglobal Mavic 3 pro. 🚁 The last shot with the glacier is from right after I landed my drone, trying to make the most of the remaining battery and light during blue hour.

#iceland

01 — No Gravity 

Two figures descending through a beam of light.

No fins. No bubbles. Nothing to tell you which way is up.

For a second, they could be underwater — or somewhere far beyond it.

02 — Suspended

Right in the middle of the light.

Not swimming up or diving down. Just suspended there, observing.

Sometimes the smallest movement would completely change the composition, so the best thing to do was simply… stay still.

03 — In motion

Some places are difficult to explain with a photograph alone.

The movement of the light, the blue filling the cave, the bodies appearing and disappearing into the darkness.

This is what it actually felt like inside.

04 — The setup

Sony α7 V + 16–35mm f/2.8.

Wide enough to show the scale of the cave, while still keeping the human figure present in the frame.

For this series, almost everything was about finding the right position between darkness, light and subject.

05 — Falling into dark

A body floating after the jump.

For a few seconds, there is no direction and almost no control — just momentum slowly disappearing into the water.

Those are usually the moments I like photographing most.

06 — One breath

A single bubble making its way back to the surface.

A tiny detail inside a huge space.

Sometimes that is all a frame needs.

07 — After everyone leaves

No divers. No movement.

Just a beam of sunlight cutting through the darkness.

The same scene that made every photograph before it possible.

Life through a disposable camera 📸😍

Os dejo una serie de fotos analógicas hechas con una cámara de usar y tirar, algo que siempre me gusta hacer en mis viajes para guardar recuerdos de una forma diferente.

Muchas veces, cuando revelas las fotos, te encuentras con momentos que ni siquiera recordabas haber capturado, y de repente esas imágenes te transportan de nuevo a ese instante, a ese lugar y a todo lo que estabas viviendo.

Soy bastante fan de las cámaras de usar y tirar precisamente por eso: nunca sabes exactamente qué vas a encontrar hasta que revelas el carrete. Y creo que ahí está parte de su magia.

Aquí os dejo una pequeña selección de algunos de mis últimos viajes, después de revelar mi última cámara 📸❤️

BASS CANYON: THRU MY EYES 🔊

Every time I come to the Gorge, I feel so incredibly refreshed and inspired to live life. The canyon view is already so jaw-dropping by itself, but when it lays behind the main stage it almost transforms into a painting.

One of my favorite things to do is sit at the top of hill overlooking the crowd and watch closely for all the cute, tiny interactions between everyone. Almost like deep breath, it’s one of the few festivals where I really can take in all the beautiful memories as they come in. 

I’m not quite sure if there’s another place like it in the world. Especially when you combine it with music from some of the best bass artists in the scene and all my amazing friends, it’s really hard for me not to keep coming back.

This video is a reflection of all that stored intimate energy being released into the canyon. Enjoy!

Rolling down a hill on a skateboard and shooting at an aperture of f1.2 was a challenge. But luckily the @dji_ronin RS4 Mini helps keen everything stable and in frame!

My two tips for nailing this kind of shot:

1. You can half press the record button on the gimbal to lock focus. I did this every time I passed a moving object so my camera didn’t autofocus on the bush. 
2. To activate the tracking module, you can single press the trigger on the front of the gimbal. Instead of using it for the entire shot, I activated it right at the end of the video when the runner was behind me, so I could focus on looking forwards.

Living in Exmouth, Western Australia, I encounter tiger sharks regularly while photographing the waters of Ningaloo Reef. For years, I had hoped to capture an image of a tiger shark approaching me out of curiosity, but without using bait such encounters are uncommon in an ecosystem where food is abundant.
On the day this photograph was made, I was swimming at the surface while following a tiger shark several metres below. After a few minutes of photographing the animal from above, it suddenly turned and swam directly toward me. Focused on composing the image, I continued shooting as it closed the distance.
Moments later, the shark briefly took the dome port of my camera into its mouth before immediately releasing it and disappearing into the blue. So focused on making the photographs, I barely registered what had happened. Only when reviewing the images later did I see how the encounter had unfolded. Having followed the shark closely for several minutes, I may have prompted its response; the brief contact appeared exploratory rather than aggressive, as the shark investigated an unfamiliar object in its environment.

100 personas. 1 dugong. Y yo fui parte del problema 🫣😮‍💨🤯🦭

Viajé hasta Egipto con la ilusión de fotografiar a uno de los animales más increíbles del océano: el dugong, una especie de vaca marina 😁

Pero lo que encontré me dejó completamente decepcionado.

Más de 100 personas rodeándolo, chapaleando, tocándolo, persiguiéndolo e invadiendo constantemente su espacio mientras intentaba alimentarse.

Y yo estaba ahí. Si bien me retiré en cuanto vi esa escena, decidí volver, grabarla y hacer este video 😮‍💨

Había pagado por esa experiencia sin investigar realmente cómo se hacía.

Ese día entendí algo: no todo turismo de naturaleza es turismo responsable.🫪

Antes de reservar una experiencia con animales salvajes, investiguemos quién la opera, cuántas personas lleva y qué protocolos tiene.

Porque querer ver un animal no debe significar molestarlo.

Si quieres conocer el dugong de una manera más responsable, comenta “DUGONG” y te digo con quién hacerlo. 🐋💙

Это все еще Китай. Просто тот, который мы почти никогда не видим 🇨🇳

На самом юге провинции Юньнань находится Хунхэ - регион, о котором до этой поездки я ничего не знал 🤔

И именно здесь находятся те самые рисовые террасы народа хани. Они спускаются по горам на километры, вокруг стоят традиционные деревни с домами, похожими на грибы, а многие вещи, которые сегодня кажутся туристическим опытом, для местных остаются частью обычной жизни 🌾

Наверное, поэтому это место так сильно отличается от привычных красивых локаций. Здесь хочется не просто приехать, снять кадр и уехать, а реально посмотреть, как все устроено 👀 

📍 Что сохранить для поездки в Хунхэ:

🌾 Yuanyang Hani Rice Terraces - те самые огромные рисовые террасы
🏘 Azheke Village - традиционная деревня народа хани среди террас
🎣 попробовать местную рыбалку прямо среди рисовых полей
🧶 познакомиться с традиционным прядением и ремеслами хани
🏠 увидеть знаменитые «грибные» дома
🪷 водная прогулка среди тысяч лотосов
🍜 Mengzi - попробовать лапшу «через мост» на ее родине
🚂 Bisezhai Railway Station - историческая станция старой Юньнань–Вьетнамской железной дороги

Еще одно напоминание, насколько огромным и разным может быть Китай 🙃
